newsitem.title: UK: Firming Bulgaria dominates figure-wary Bradys.
newsitem.headline: Firming Bulgaria dominates figure-wary Bradys.

text.p: Bulgaria, its tarnished star looking slightly shinier, rose in an emerging debt market that otherwise did little as investors waited for U.S. economic data on Friday, traders said.
"Bulgaria is the only one really trading. But it's more down to buying by one, maybe two, funds," a European bank trader said.

He said that without that interest, news alone that the International Monetary Fund could well increase its loans to Bulgaria would have had not much less impact on the market, with views on the outlook of the economy still very wary.
Bulgarian FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were bid at 38-5/8, up 7/8 on from the New York close. The price has risen more than 1-1/2 points since Wednesday.
Earlier, Bulgarian officials said that IMF would significantly increase the amount of money it would lend the country if Sofia introduced a currency board.
There was an early fall in Russian MinFins but prices recovered some of their lost ground later in the morning.
Elsewhere, the market was very subdued as it waited for Friday's U.S. payroll data.
Bradys managed to hold up well despite Wednesday's slip in U.S. Treasuries, but there is concern that the long bond may have already reached its peak, one trader said.
Some traders are still hoping for a return of buying before the end of the year, though others are more cautious.
"People have had a good year. They don't want any hiccups and start January or February in a hole," senior Bank of America trader Michael Jordan said.
Latin American debt was barely touched in London, including Ecaudor which had weakened on Wednesday on confusion over the state of economic reform.
But ABN-AMRO Latin American analyst, Ian Campbell, said spreads on Ecuadorian Bradys were likely to tighten futher despite worries about the convertibility plan.

"If Congress passes the bulk of (President Abdala) Bucaram's measures and dates are set for the first privatisations, the bonds will trade up," he said, but a added there would be a steep fall if reforms stalled.
